experiment: MDLM Sigma-Guided Diffusion on Apple MPS

model.name: kuleshov-group/mdlm-owt
model.paper: Simple and Effective Masked Diffusion Language Models (NeurIPS 2024)

key_finding.description: Sigma-guided step selection significantly outperforms uniform step reduction at the SAME compute cost

sigma_profile_insight.description: Sigma (KL divergence between consecutive timestep predictions) is strongly concentrated in early steps (high t, near pure noise)
sigma_profile_insight.interpretation: Most information gain happens when the model first sees through the noise. Later steps contribute negligible information.

honest_caveats: Baseline PPL has high variance (one outlier at 248.17), likely due to degenerate generation
Sigma-guided uses a fixed profile from a single profiling run -- the profile itself is stochastic
The sigma-guided approach requires a profiling pass (one-time cost) before generation
MPS float32 may behave differently from CUDA bf16/fp16 in the original paper
seq_len=256 is shorter than the model default of 1024; results may differ at full length
Sigma values are very small in absolute terms (1e-5 to 1e-8), but their RELATIVE differences drive the selection

connection_to_petz_theory.description: This experiment validates the core insight from the Petz recovery framework applied to discrete diffusion
connection_to_petz_theory.key_equation: Sigma = D(rho_t || rho_{t-dt}) = KL divergence between model predictions at consecutive timesteps
connection_to_petz_theory.prediction: Steps with higher Sigma contribute more information (harder to recover from), so they should be preserved
connection_to_petz_theory.result: Confirmed -- keeping high-Sigma steps and skipping low-Sigma steps produces BETTER text than uniform sampling
connection_to_petz_theory.petz_bound: F >= exp(-Sigma/2) means low-Sigma steps have recovery fidelity F near 1 (information is preserved without the step)
